title: Sentinel Ledger: certifiable KV eviction for mixed TTL/LRU workloads
creator: Aisha Banerjee
description: Proposal and implementation tracker for a new "Sentinel Ledger" eviction subsystem designed to provide certifiable correctness guarantees across mixed TTL and LRU eviction strategies while preserving prefix isolation semantics for multi-tenant KV caching on GPU-backed inference nodes. Targets continuous batching workloads where KV lifetime and memory pressure are highly variable. The ledger is a lightweight, append-only operation log (sentinels) that records invalidation intent, atomic lease handoffs, and prefix-scoped checkpoints so that eviction can be replayed and audited off-path. Goals: 1) Avoid prefix-corruption during partial evictions under concurrency and batching; 2) Prove invariants that evicted prefixes never reappear with stale KV pointers; 3) Minimize GPU memory stalls and fragmentation by enabling compact reclamation windows; 4) Provide runtime hooks for canary rollouts and emergency rollback to safe LRU-only mode.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc approved by Runtime and Storage leads
Prototype ledger implemented with <5% median inference latency regression under 128QPS continuous batching load
Unit + integration tests that simulate concurrent prefix-scoped eviction, lease transfer, and replay produce zero detected stale-read anomalies over 10k simulated traces
Benchmark demonstrating <3% additional GPU memory overhead for sentinel metadata at 16M KV entries
Canary rollout plan validated: automated fallback to LRU-only policy within 60s on detected correctness violation
progress_updates: 2025-02-11: Kickoff meeting. Agreed scope: ledger is append-only, stored off-GPU in host memory with compact checkpoint snapshots pushed to GPU at configurable cadence.
2025-02-13: Chose representation for sentinels: 64-bit sentinel records (prefix_id, op_type, seq, lease_id) to keep footprint minimal. Trade-off: longer replay time vs smaller RAM/GPU overhead.

2025-02-16: Prototype eviction coordinator written. Coordinator serializes eviction intents per-prefix and issues 'soft-invalidate' sentinel before reclaiming KV buckets to allow in-flight requests to finish.

2025-02-18: Integration test harness added: stressbench simulating continuous batching with bursty sequence lengths and mixed TTL distributions. Observed transient tail latency spike when checkpoint frequency = 1s; tuning in progress.
2025-02-20: Design review feedback from Security: require signed sentinel digests for Private deployments (KMS-backed). Added spec for optional digest signing and audit export.

2025-02-24: Formal invariants drafted and initial model-checking runs completed (bounded traces). Found and fixed race where concurrent lease handoff + TTL expiry could cause stale pointer resurrection in corner case.
2025-02-25: Preparing GitHub PR for prototype (see prs entry). Next: expand integration tests and run large-scale simulation on staging cluster.
tests: fuzz: eviction-replay-fuzzer (seed corpus from production traces)
perf: staged 128QPS continuous-batching run with and without ledger
risks: Metadata overhead: sentinel records add host-memory pressure; mitigation: compact encoding + periodic checkpointing to discard old sentinels
Replay latency: long replay windows can stall reclamation; mitigation: incremental checkpointing and prioritized garbage collection
Complexity: added eviction coordinator increases code surface for concurrency bugs; mitigation: model checking and staged rollout with LRU-only fallback
Performance regressions in tight latency SLOs during checkpoint flush; mitigation: adaptive checkpointing tied to observed tail latency
next_steps: Complete PRs and run full staging harness (expected by 2025-03-03)
Add KMS-signed sentinel digests and audit-export in Private builds
Coordinate with Console team for metrics: eviction-audit-events, sentinel-replay-duration, and stale-read-detection-rate
Plan canary: 2% of tenant traffic on Dedicated for 48h, automated rollback triggers configured
